newsitem.title: UK: BFI rise slows, but may not have ended.
newsitem.headline: BFI rise slows, but may not have ended.

text.p: The Baltic Freight Index (BFI) rose 13 points on Tuesday to 1,515 points, a relatively small increase by recent standards as the Panamax market paused for breath.

Brokers opinion was divided about whether the Panamax market was now levelling off but reports indicated that a heavy volume of orders has still to be covered before Christmas, especially in the Atlantic.
In the Far East South Korean charterers were reported to have fixed Atlantic Sovereign 68,000 dwt delivery retrospectively North Japan yesterday for Pacific round at $13,750 daily.
A number of Panamaxes have also been booked for periods up to two years timecharter at rates between $9,000 and $11,000 daily.

The slowing of upward momentum in the underlying market saw BIFFEX rates take a dive, with early 1997 months particularly weak, and losses ranged by 1300 GMT ranging from 18 to 91 points. Turnover totalled 237 lots.
